Whatsoever
It is a diverse neighborhood. A lot of lower income familes. The parks are not well kept and there is a lot of trash
It is a very diverse neighborhood. You’ll find whites, Spanish, black, Asian here. It is a great neighborhood but a lot of times, there a lot of reports of killings, stealings, and fire
I like the diversity in cultures, people and how safe the environment is. The train stations are well preserved and there’s less crime going on in the environment. People are kind and friendly
I love the neighboor hood although sometimes there may be dangers outside or people from all over the place jamaica is a big family and has a very diverse, connected, and supportive community.
I would say that Jamaica is an ok place. you're able to leave your house and find something to do. Jamaica ave never gets quiet either.

I became a frequent visitor to Jamaica Queens when I was job hunting- for any opportunities that may be useful as I was going through a divorce. In October 2025 my divorce was final and I began to search for a shelter for my kids and I. I found ICNA Relief Transitional Home for women which is a great place to get help. They offer food pantry every Thursday- feel free to come get some fresh foods!
Jamaica gives me this opportunity and accessibility vibes. Almost every and any government establishment like courts, HRA offices, most banks, hospitals are close by with either a walking distance or a few stops with the train or bus. It's so easy for me commute to destinations in time. The diversity is really nice with different shades of colors, languages, cultures and food! The downside is some parts Jamaica can be really dirty, especially outside of street cleaning hours. It is often common to find homeless or mentally disabled people in the streets which may be frightening for kids.

Jamaica Queens provides an interesting mix of cultural diversity, dynamism, and hustle. The area is one of the most transit-oriented areas in Queens that provides numerous transportation services such as LIRR and subways that makes it easy for people to travel to Manhattan and elsewhere in NYC. In addition, this neighborhood is characterized by diverse culture due to the presence of many individuals representing various ethnicities. Different cultures can be observed by analyzing the variety of food and local businesses. The aspect of life for this community is dynamism since there is always some activity going on at any point in time. There are numerous local businesses, many streets with street vendors selling their products and food as well as many pedestrians who are constantly walking around and creating this fun atmosphere. However, despite the positive sides that characterize neighborhood, it should be said that it is noisy and crowded with some safety issues.
Very diverse place. Transportation is a big help with commuting. Not very safe at night. Hard to find a nice place to rent that isnt super expensive.

My neighborhood is a generally interesting one; it's diversified in many regions, but the main one is the apartment buildings. Everyone as a whole in the neighborhood is friendly. One thing I would like to change is the lack of bus service going through the area; in the past you could get a bus every 5-10 minutes, but now it's around every 10-20 minutes depending on what time you leave your house.

Jamaica is a nice area to live in. However, the downfall of the area is the commute from the city. While the city is where most people commute from, it is a bit of a hassle if you travel via Subway as opposed to the LIRR. I will say the transit hub is amazing as you're close to JFK. I do wish there were more local businesses as I feel that franchises have taken over.

I feel like nightlife could be a lot better in Jamaica Queens, but the culture is unmatched and it is a melting pot of people like no other. Queens is a great place to settle down, but it is also a great place for varying ages.

If you like a community that would look out for one another then I would suggest taking a visit to Jamaica, NY. Though recent construction has demolished old buildings that once were, for the most part the neighborhood looks exactly the same as it was since I was a kid. There is a rich history here that I haven't fully explored myself but from the conversations I have had with people on the bus or walking by tells me that there is much to explore within my neighborhood. Traffic here is the worst especially during rush hours, so that would probably be my first suggestion for change in this neighborhood. With any new place it is also understood that you remain aware of your surroundings but other then that enjoy.

I would definitely like to see the level of education within Jamaica rise, with either more schools propping up or more funding provided to grant schools greater access to top-tier resources and facilities for their students, like maker spaces or computer labs.
I like that I can always just hop on the train to go anywhere; I don't have to take an Uber everywhere I need to go. I would like to see the gang activity die down on Jamaica Avenue
The streets are a bit sketchy, especially at night, but when with friends it's okay. The food scene is great.

Living in Jamaica, Queens has been a very mixed experience. I like that it’s diverse, full of culture, and has so many food options from around the world. Transportation is convenient with the subway and LIRR nearby. What I’d like to see change is improved safety, cleaner streets, and more community spaces for young people.

Living in Jamaica is a very efficient and ideal experience. There are many different forms of transportation here which makes the area and other areas very accessible. There are many entertainment options and basic necessities.

Jamaica Queens New York is such great place to live. Deep in culture, love and pride. The accessibility to all the other outer boroughs and long island make it a very central place to live. Jamaica has its spotty parts, but overall its a nice place to live. People in my area have a sense of pride about our neighborhood. From the busy streets of Jamaica Ave to the beautiful park of Kings Park, the plays at the black spectrum theater, the dollar vans that take you from east to west, and the Airtran to JFK airport to help beat the traffic on the Van Wyck. Pizza at Margherita, and the Queens library all offer such a bright vibrant experience. As a woman born and raised in Jamaica I gleam with pride telling people where is come from and how far I have gone. The public schools are amazing and the teachers really love and nurture the children.

Briarwood is extremely welcoming and overall a great community. There are many things to do and many opportunities.

I am a licensed real estate salesperson who has worked in the Briarwood area for about 10 years, and I must say, it has become one of my favorite neighborhoods in Queens. This tree-lined street has all the Queens charm I grew up with.
Briarwood offers numerous commuting options: it is close to highways, subways, buses, and has clear bike lanes. As an avid bicyclist, I love riding down for my showings. The neighborhood features a great mixture of residential houses, rental buildings, and co-ops, which reflects its diversity.
The public park is always bustling, and both Forest Park and Flushing Meadow Park are not too far away. Many of my past clients who have moved into the neighborhood love the change.

I moved to briarwood in march and absolutely love it. It is still extremely affordable yet homey and close to everything. The F train is a so close by as is multiple highways and buses. I really love the atmosphere and how diverse the neighborhood is.

Briarwood is a small quiet neighborhood. You know the people in your building and those who work there. The small neighborhood has every store you can need with a subway station that can bring you further into Queens or all the way to Brooklyn.

As many others have stated, Briarwood is pleasant enough. I'm a single female and have never felt unsafe here at any time of the day or night. Little to no crime. Centrally located so it's not too far from Manhattan, LI or Brooklyn depending on your mode of transport. Express bus to Manhattan in 35 mins, LIRR to BK and or LI in 20 mins and LIRR to Penn Station in less than 20 mins. Several bus routes and the E/F station. Located near multiple highways. Parking is challenging. There aren't very many activities or entertainment but close enough to neighborhoods which have those options (Forest Hills, Jamaica, Kew Gardens). Very few supermarkets, grocery stores and restaurants and options are not very good. Very diverse, but I don't necessarily find the residents very friendly or welcoming. No real community feel. If you can afford it go to Kew Gardens or Forest Hills.

Briarwood is a hidden gem! I lived here 3 years and loved it. There are so many trees and its quiet and safe. You can even see the stars which is a treat for NYC. We felt like coming back to our own oasis from Manhattan. We had a great private landlord who was great. Loved the diversity. Didn't spend much time in the neighborhood for entertainment. E/F were reliable and fast to the city. Eventually moved to be closer to the city but honestly miss briarwood a lot. Great access to forest park for biking and close to LIRR. the neighbors keep to themselves and after 3 years only started feeling little more connected. But it was also during covid so yeah. I really recommend briarwood to anyone who is looking for a diverse, safe, quiet, and tree filled neighborhood. :) It's small which I think there's pride in it too- not many people know about it! But some ppl think it's too far. Find what works for you! Albas pizza is great and close walk to dani pizza and Mr. Wish BBT.
I like how quite and peaceful the neighbor hoods are. Very friendly and cleaned. And schools are also nice and big.

Excellent place to live if you work in Manhattan, especially UES and midtown, quick express subway ride. Affordable housing if you want to buy a cooperative, 1 & 2 bedrooms, more spacious than the Astoria and Woodside coops. Has everything but nightlife, but Forest Hills is close. Good food options, grocery, fruit/veg shops and excellent pizza place. Safe. And nicely diverse, without one taking over. Up and coming d/t reasonable housing.

Briarwood is the place my wife and i got our first apartment, we have raised a daughter here who is now in college. i love the diversity of the neighborhood although there are some here who still wish it was not so diverse. Transportation is excellent parking sucks, and there is not a whole lot of stuff to do, but it’s a quiet great place to raise a family in a city like New York. There is a decent amount of choice for food, a decent amount of bodegas and a very decent diner. yeah all in all it’s just a great place to lay your head at night in peace.
great community and the people are really friendly. wish there were more things nearby though but love it. been living here my whole life.
Tired of dealing with my racist neighbors. Tired of stepping in dog poop everywhere. Can we start on the fact that everything here is so overpriced?

I have lived in Briarwood all of my life. My neighbors have always been welcoming. Late at night, it can feel unsafe. However, I have not felt safer in any other neighborhood that I have visited in NYC. There are many places to shop for clothing and groceries, and countless busses and trains all within short ranges of each other so you can go wherever whenever.

This area is nothing crazy. It has a plentiful amount of eateries which is wonderful, but it is lacking in effectively every other entertainment area. That said, the neighborhood has all kinds of necessities covered and you will not need to go far from the area if you live there. Transportation-wise, Briarwood has good coverage in the F line and with the Q44/Q60. So despite its lack of some things, getting to an area that has what you're looking for is generally simple. The community is relatively quiet and pleasantly diverse. If you're looking for a setting to step away from the city life, this neighborhood might be the perfect one for you.
The only issue about the area that I live in is that the MTA train station is not near my house. Also, the streets are not straight and you have to be careful when you walk.
I love the quietness and peace there is in Briarwood and how the community is kept relatively clean. I also love how every neighbor minds their own business.
Briarwood is a great neighborhood. There isn't much to do around the neighborhood, but there is easy access to the train and public transportation making it fast and easy to get to any area.

Very residential area, great because train stop is centrally located and on the F/E line. Local library lacks a little, but that is okay because you can request any book from the Queens library system online and have it sent to your local branch. Schools are okay, parks are nice, restaurants are a little lacking, but plenty close by at Austin Street.

I think Briarwood is an amazing place to live because of the people, easy access to public transportation, and diversity of stores. I do not like how Briarwood is a destination location and people who come here only come with one purpose or because they live here
Great neighborhood to raise a young family. Parks nearby and many choices in schooling from daycares to High Schools!

Jamaica Hills is known for its diversity. As a long time resident, I noticed the neighborhood diversified significantly where multiple homeowners and tenants come from different backgrounds. Captain Tilly Park is the heart of our neighborhood where it brings neighbors together. As the President of Jamaica Hill Community Association, I observed that neighbors will get along with you if you share common values. Getting involved in the community is the one best way to carry pride for our community. Our civic association engages our community with many activities all year long. Our icons, George Tilly named after him as Captain Tilly Park, Sri Chimnoy, J Cole, Queens Borough President Donavan Richards Jr. , Including Janice Zarchi founding member of JHCA and a family member of Hollywood Producers and actors/actresses left a legacy or became successful after living or going to school in the area. Although our neighborhood is quiet, but it is a neighborhood for beacon of opportunities.
12 years I’m living in this neighborhood, neighbors are very friendly. Zone schools are A+. Most of the neighbors are Asian.

I've been living here all my life. It's a very diverse neighborhood, also welcoming. Many people know each other, and cooperate within the community to make it a better place. Jamaica Hills is one of the most popular and welcoming community in Queens.
Most houses are occupied because of the great neighborhood. Cost of housing and utilities are average.
The community is tranquil and peaceful. Not too many community events to engage in. Definitely pet friendly.
No crimes for the past four years I've been living here. A couple of highway accidents, but that's about it.
Very peaceful and solitude. No crimes. Easy access to public transportation, schools, local retailers and restaurants.

whenever I come from work, approximately 2 minutes from my house, Folks are hanging out in front of the house that seems like two house where a few units exist. I can smell so much of marihuana. Also, When I get off from subway, People are hanging out on the corner and street, which seems unpleasant as well

I think my area seems very quiet and no new residents are coming in. But whenever I commute by subway or bus, the area that I need to pass by to use transportation is always dirty and garbages are everywhere, especially around subway station which could be better cleaned by government's tax.
Particularly by me I don't hear crime stories or anything of that nature

Apart from the crowded streets and too much traffic, i love the place i live in because its very convenient and all shops are nearby. The subways, bus stops, restaurants and departmental stores are right at the corner making life easier.
The houses are mostly in good conditions with the exceptions of some
Physical activities is not much of a problem here because there is YMCA 5 min away and 2 parks near by
There is not much outdoor activities
There not many crimes that happen. However, I would not recommend walking late at night just in case I would rather be safe than sorry.
It is like a typical New York City weather. It snows in the winter and hot in the summer

People that live here are from all background and there isn't a particular job that most of them do. However the home owners make a good amount of money because the houses here are pretty expensive for a middle class person
There is barely any resturants
There are a bunch of local grocery stores that people constantly buy stuff from because its close to their homes.

Overall, Kew Gardens is a nice safe neighborhood for a family. I live in Kew Gardens now, but have lived other places and can say it is much quieter and safer than others. However, in the last few years, this nice safe neighborhood has taken a very minor dip on the not so safe end but that’s more towards the courthouse area of the neighborhood. Overall, Kew Gardens is a great place to live.

I definitely feel like it could be cleaned up more. There're a lot of commuters that come out of the subway and leave their trash all over the streets, the neighborhood could definitely be cleaned up near where there're high amounts of traffic whether it's foot or car.

I moved to Kew Gardens 7 years ago. It's quiet at night, there are enough things to do in the immediate area (sit-down restaurants, outdoor dining, cafes, bank, pharmacies, hair salons, independent movie theater, day spa, etc.), the library is a close walk, and it's pretty quiet at night, especially for NYC. My favorite spots are Cookies and Cream Pastry Shop, Ascend Day Spa, Kew Gardens Cinemas, and Dani's Pizza. I really like that it's ethnically diverse, dog-friendly, and LGBTQ-friendly. I have never been cat-called here and no one has said anything anti-gay toward me or my spouse which unfortunately was not my experience in other neighborhoods. I feel that the people are much more down-to-earth here compared to some other NYC neighborhoods. I have several neighbors that I consider actual friends. If you have a dog, you will meet a ton of people. Depending on exactly where you are in KG, you may walk a bit to the LIRR or subway, but there are plenty of bus stops.

One of the standout features of Kew Gardens is its abundant green spaces. The crown jewel, of course, is the stunning Forest Park, which feels like a slice of paradise in the urban jungle. The expansive park offers an array of recreational activities, from picnics to hiking and biking trails. Whether you're a nature enthusiast or just looking for a peaceful escape, Forest Park is the perfect retreat.
I think Kew Gardens is a calm and peaceful neighborhood with not a lot of crime or chaos. I am privileged to live in Kew Gardens.

I've lived in Kew Gardens previously, it was a decent little town and still is but largely depends on why you would want to move here.
It's usually a pretty quiet neighborhood (though tends to be noisier along Metropolitan Ave). Very safe overall. The northern part near the subway stop and courthouse is less inviting. There are some nice houses on tree-lined streets that you don't see in many other parts of NYC that are hyper-urbanized.
There's an independent movie theater that's been here for many years, and two very good pizza fast-food places. The apartment buildings here are pretty basic and the architecture could be nicer.
A cool little town if you don't need the trendiness and hipness of Williamsburg, Astoria or other neighborhoods in NYC. It's mainly a working-class town with many flight attendants. JFK airport is pretty close to here.
The LIRR also stops here and is often a better option going to/from NYC or Long Island. The subway is a fairly long commute to Manhattan.

I have lived in Kew Gardens for over 6 years.
Pros:
Overall, it is a pretty safe neighborhood that is great for families and young professionals. Fast commute to NYC from the LIRR and the E/F subway line. Close to JFK/LGA. Good place to have a dog. Walking distance to Forest Park, restaurants, coffee shops, bakeries, laundromats, pharmacies, vets, hair salons, our local bookstore Kew & Willow Books, library, Ascend Spa and Kew Gardens Cinema. Affordable coops if you would like to own. The neighborhood is becoming more accepting of the LGBTQ+ community. Of course, there is always more room for improvement.
Cons:
Terrible place for parking if you own a car. Cars get ticketed all the time so you better follow the alternate side parking rules. Increase in catalytic converter and tire thefts. There are only two grocery stores in this neighborhood on Metropolitan Ave. You would need a car or to take a bus to Trader Joe's and Stop & Shop for a bigger selection.

Kew Gardens is a safe place for everybody. Nothing really happens that is out of the ordinary. Everybody is very kind here, the buisness owners are very nice to their customers and workers alike. The library workers are very friendly and will willing help with all requests for books and just having conversations with you.
It is a friendly and quiet neighborhood. A lot of new shops and restaurants are opening up nearby. Forest hills park is a nice escape from the busy city.

Kew Gardens used to be predominantly Jewish people, however, over the years there has been an increase in culture and races in this neighborhood. I love how there are Mexican supermarkets next to Chinese restaurants and Japanese cuisines next to beautiful parks! In addition, Kew Gardens is one of the cleaner neighborhood in queens with big streets and trash cans at every block! This is somewhere I'm proud to call home.
I've lived in Kew Gardens for 3-4 years and I have had no issues with the neighborhood i am currently living in.

Rego Park is a vibrant neighborhood with a great mix of cultures, food options, and convenient shopping. The area is well-connected with public transportation, making it easy to get to Manhattan or other parts of Queens. I love the variety of restaurants, especially the Eastern European and Central Asian spots. Rego Center provide plenty of shopping choices such as Costco and Aldi. However, traffic can be heavy, local trains available only and parking is often a challenge. Overall, it’s a decent place to live with a diverse community and plenty of amenities.

What I love: Shopping & Food: Good food and shopping, and Rego Park delivers. I’ve spent entire afternoons wandering through Rego Center and grabbing bites from the local spots. There’s this little Uzbek restaurant I discovered once, and it’s become one of my go-to places.
Convenience: Living here feels easy. The subway gets me where I need to go without too much drama, and I love that I can hop on a bus.
Community Vibes: The diversity has made me feel comfortable as a Afro-Latina, I have never had a bad experience in the neighborhood.
What could be better:
Parking Struggles: Driving here is not my favorite thing. I remember one time it took me almost 30 minutes to find a spot, and I was this close to giving up and taking the subway instead!
Needs More Green Spaces: I really wish there were more parks.
Building Maintenance: Some of the older buildings have their charm, but a little TLC wouldn’t hurt. I’ve noticed a few places that could use better upkeep.
The area is safe and family friendly. There are many shops and stores namely Marshalls, Burlington, Old Navy. Numerous restaurants and bars. All kinds of things.

I've lived here my whole life and I can say with confidence that it's a nice neighborhood. It's relatively safe and quiet. There are various public/private elementary, middle, and high schools in the area or nearby, close to a lot of public transportation going in all directions. Kids can also enjoy spending time in the many playgrounds in the surrounding area, or can also take a nice walk to Flushing Meadow Park which is close by. The subway stop is near the blvd, and you can catch a bus on almost every block going to Manhattan, Roosevelt, Flushing, Jamaica, & both the airports. It's more of a residential area for kids and seniors so there's not much nightlife, but you can catch the train or bus for those places. Food options are also pretty good and varied. We have a melting pot of cultures here with the biggest being the Buharian community so we have a lot of food options from those areas as well as Italian, Peruvian, Chinese, Colombian, Thai, etc. This place is pretty great.......
My experience has been pleasing so far. There are many restaurants and stores to go to so there's always something to do.

I have enjoyed living in rego park for the past 3 years. To be honest I was never used to living in a rowdy area per se, I was always used to quite neighborhoods but after a while I started to feel safer than I ever felt in the other places I have lived in. The crime rate is low, the community is good, overall I would not think about moving far away from Rego Park. I have transportation convenience and a store for everything around me.

There's a real old-school neighborhood feel, the neighbors get to know one another and look out for the kids. It's a great place to live.

I especially love Metropolitan Avenue since there is a CVS, Trader Joe's and even an Advantage Care.

However, quiet times leave room for peace.

I somewhat live in Flushing since I currently dorm there while attending Queens College, although my permanent home is in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, where I live with my parents. One major difference I have noticed between the two communities is the sense of safety. In Bedford-Stuyvesant, I often feel like I have to be more aware of my surroundings because there is frequently police activity and situations that can make the area feel less secure. In contrast, Flushing feels much calmer and safer overall. The environment there allows me to feel more comfortable walking outside, whether it is to get food, spend time outdoors, or simply enjoy the area. Living in both places has shown me how different communities can create very different everyday experiences.

I love Flushing. I live in an area where I have access to a LIRR train station, a bodega, a laundromat, and virtually anything at my fingertips. I see families of different backgrounds and young folks walking to and from school. It is the picturesque NYC. There is a lot of opportunity here and I am thankful for it.

Flushing can be very quiet or a bit noisy depending on the area you're in. I appreciate the abundance of stores that make buying certain things more convenient. However, some areas could use more support or consistent maintenance to insure all parts of the neighborhood are as safe, clean and good as they can be.

I've known Flushing for a very long time from birth up until now. Overall, it's one of the greatest chinatowns in the country. The fact that a lot of immigrants from China would rather occupy Flushing instead of the other chinatown in manhattan just makes Flushing the king of chinese immigrants.
Crowds are common near the 7 train station and the long island rail road, so I recommend being cautious when walking on main street.
Also, street vendors and smoking cigarettes is common so there's that.

When people ask about Flushing, I provide the answer: "Flushing is nice to visit but, a terrible place to live." I live in the downtown area and due to overcrowding, it is absolutely filthy. More so than any other area of NYC (and I have experience living in various parts of the city). As a result, garbage litters the sidewalks on a daily basis and the stench is overwhelming. Furthermore, we are 1.8 miles from LGA and the airplanes often fly low and frequently overhead. The noise is deafening and poses a serious issue that has made the news (Google: Tennis Climb flight path). People also smoke CONSTANTLY around here. Parking is almost nonexistent. The positives of Flushing are the beautiful Kissena Park, and it has a great gym/shopping centers. There are also many great places to eat and it is overall a safe neighborhood. Nevertheless, I do not feel the pros make up for the cons. Sadly, the quality of life here is abysmal. If you value quiet and cleanliness, do not move here.

I have been living in flushing all my life, and so far it is gradually becoming a not so safe neighborhood. As of recently there were a few incidents that happened over here in flushing. It is a convenient place due to everything being near by.

My husband and I wanted a chance to visit the 911 Memorial, see Broadway show and ride the ferry amongst others things. Flushing was an affordable stay and had easy access to the city Manhattan and to the other boroughs via subway. We had everything we needed there. It felt safe and the food was amazing if you love Asian cuisine. We totally enjoyed our stay there and will go again.

The best of all worlds - close enough to the city for easy access by subway, bus, LIRR but far enough to feel suburban without being out on the island. We have it all - great food, great parks, great living, great activities. It's a little crowded in some parts but overall neighbors know neighbors but you don't feel like you're living in a fishbowl

Living in Flushing has been a unique and enriching experience. I really enjoy how culturally diverse the neighborhood is—there’s always something new to try, from amazing food spots to community festivals. The area feels lively and connected, and you get to meet people from all kinds of backgrounds.
If there’s one thing I’d like to see improve, it would be the traffic and crowding, especially around Main Street. It can get pretty hectic. But overall, Flushing has a lot of heart, and it’s a place that really reflects the energy of New York City.

My overall experience with Flushing has been positive. It's a vibrant, diverse neighborhood with incredible food options, especially for Asian cuisine. The area can get crowded at times, but it's well-connected by public transportation and has everything you need nearby—grocery stores, parks, and cultural spots. While it’s a bit busy, that energy is part of what makes it unique.

I've lived in Flushing my whole life and I'm glad that I did. Flushing has a large Chinese population, thus it may be referred to as a "Little Chinatown" or such. With this large Chinese population, a lot of Chinas culture and traditions have been implemented. My favorite thing personally is the food, the food in Flushing is absolutely amazing and I think one thing Flushing has a lot of are Bubble Tea stores and Hot Pot Franchises. Another thing about Flushing is that it is very very crowded, some days it can be better but on the weekends the area is usually bustling, and something I have been seeing is that more people from different backgrounds are shopping and working and overall are around the area, which makes me happy that Flushing may provide a greater aspect to share Chinese culture. Overall I love Flushing and it will always have a place in my heart with all the memories I hold there, but something I would definitely want to see change is the cleanliness and crowding.

Living in Flushing has been a unique and memorable experience. It’s a neighborhood filled with cultural richness, diversity, and non-stop energy. I’ve had the chance to try cuisines I never would have discovered elsewhere. Beyond food, Flushing feels alive every day of the week, with busy markets, local businesses, and people from all walks of life coming together. It’s also accessible with public transportation, which makes it easy to get around. However, I do think the area could benefit from improved cleanliness, better traffic management, and more green space. Despite those challenges, Flushing has helped me grow, stay connected to a broader world, and appreciate community life in a way few places can offer. I’m grateful for the time I’ve spent here.

The neighborhood always feels lively and welcoming. One thing I would like to see improve is less traffic and overcrowding, especially during busy hours. Overall, Flushing is a vibrant community with a lot to offer.

I somewhat live in Flushing since I currently dorm there while attending Queens College, although my permanent home is in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, where I live with my parents. One major difference I have noticed between the two communities is the sense of safety. In Bedford-Stuyvesant, I often feel like I have to be more aware of my surroundings because there is frequently police activity and situations that can make the area feel less secure. In contrast, Flushing feels much calmer and safer overall. The environment there allows me to feel more comfortable walking outside, whether it is to get food, spend time outdoors, or simply enjoy the area. Living in both places has shown me how different communities can create very different everyday experiences.

I love Flushing. I live in an area where I have access to a LIRR train station, a bodega, a laundromat, and virtually anything at my fingertips. I see families of different backgrounds and young folks walking to and from school. It is the picturesque NYC. There is a lot of opportunity here and I am thankful for it.

Flushing can be very quiet or a bit noisy depending on the area you're in. I appreciate the abundance of stores that make buying certain things more convenient. However, some areas could use more support or consistent maintenance to insure all parts of the neighborhood are as safe, clean and good as they can be.

I've known Flushing for a very long time from birth up until now. Overall, it's one of the greatest chinatowns in the country. The fact that a lot of immigrants from China would rather occupy Flushing instead of the other chinatown in manhattan just makes Flushing the king of chinese immigrants.
Crowds are common near the 7 train station and the long island rail road, so I recommend being cautious when walking on main street.
Also, street vendors and smoking cigarettes is common so there's that.

When people ask about Flushing, I provide the answer: "Flushing is nice to visit but, a terrible place to live." I live in the downtown area and due to overcrowding, it is absolutely filthy. More so than any other area of NYC (and I have experience living in various parts of the city). As a result, garbage litters the sidewalks on a daily basis and the stench is overwhelming. Furthermore, we are 1.8 miles from LGA and the airplanes often fly low and frequently overhead. The noise is deafening and poses a serious issue that has made the news (Google: Tennis Climb flight path). People also smoke CONSTANTLY around here. Parking is almost nonexistent. The positives of Flushing are the beautiful Kissena Park, and it has a great gym/shopping centers. There are also many great places to eat and it is overall a safe neighborhood. Nevertheless, I do not feel the pros make up for the cons. Sadly, the quality of life here is abysmal. If you value quiet and cleanliness, do not move here.

I have been living in flushing all my life, and so far it is gradually becoming a not so safe neighborhood. As of recently there were a few incidents that happened over here in flushing. It is a convenient place due to everything being near by.

My husband and I wanted a chance to visit the 911 Memorial, see Broadway show and ride the ferry amongst others things. Flushing was an affordable stay and had easy access to the city Manhattan and to the other boroughs via subway. We had everything we needed there. It felt safe and the food was amazing if you love Asian cuisine. We totally enjoyed our stay there and will go again.

The best of all worlds - close enough to the city for easy access by subway, bus, LIRR but far enough to feel suburban without being out on the island. We have it all - great food, great parks, great living, great activities. It's a little crowded in some parts but overall neighbors know neighbors but you don't feel like you're living in a fishbowl

Living in Flushing has been a unique and enriching experience. I really enjoy how culturally diverse the neighborhood is—there’s always something new to try, from amazing food spots to community festivals. The area feels lively and connected, and you get to meet people from all kinds of backgrounds.
If there’s one thing I’d like to see improve, it would be the traffic and crowding, especially around Main Street. It can get pretty hectic. But overall, Flushing has a lot of heart, and it’s a place that really reflects the energy of New York City.

My overall experience with Flushing has been positive. It's a vibrant, diverse neighborhood with incredible food options, especially for Asian cuisine. The area can get crowded at times, but it's well-connected by public transportation and has everything you need nearby—grocery stores, parks, and cultural spots. While it’s a bit busy, that energy is part of what makes it unique.

I've lived in Flushing my whole life and I'm glad that I did. Flushing has a large Chinese population, thus it may be referred to as a "Little Chinatown" or such. With this large Chinese population, a lot of Chinas culture and traditions have been implemented. My favorite thing personally is the food, the food in Flushing is absolutely amazing and I think one thing Flushing has a lot of are Bubble Tea stores and Hot Pot Franchises. Another thing about Flushing is that it is very very crowded, some days it can be better but on the weekends the area is usually bustling, and something I have been seeing is that more people from different backgrounds are shopping and working and overall are around the area, which makes me happy that Flushing may provide a greater aspect to share Chinese culture. Overall I love Flushing and it will always have a place in my heart with all the memories I hold there, but something I would definitely want to see change is the cleanliness and crowding.

Living in Flushing has been a unique and memorable experience. It’s a neighborhood filled with cultural richness, diversity, and non-stop energy. One of the things I’ve appreciated most is the wide variety of food options, there are so many authentic restaurants, bakeries, and food stands that reflect the neighborhood’s global character, especially its strong Asian influence. I’ve had the chance to try cuisines I never would have discovered elsewhere. Beyond food, Flushing feels alive every day of the week, with busy markets, local businesses, and people from all walks of life coming together. It’s also accessible with public transportation, which makes it easy to get around. However, I do think the area could benefit from improved cleanliness, better traffic management, and more green space. Despite those challenges, Flushing has helped me grow, stay connected to a broader world, and appreciate community life in a way few places can offer. I’m grateful for the time I’ve spent here.

Growing up in Flushing, NY was a very immersive experience being surrounded by such a diverse population. Additionally going out to eat was a lot of fun because there was so many options to choose from because of the cultural impact.

its a pretty safe place to live in, you can encounter a lot of natural life and parks around. you feel safe running at night see a lot of dogs and find yourself in a quiet and pleasant neighborhood , its really easy to find apartments and things to do around her, its near a mall and many local shops with activities so you'll never find yourself bored.

I was born and raised in Middle Village, and I couldn’t think of any where else I would prefer to live. Middle Village has an amazing sense of community, beautiful scenery and many great attributes including Juniper Valley Park. the only big issues I've seen personally is the amount of time fallen tree branches that require machinery to be moved are left in place before anyone can do anything

Middle Village is a nice neighborhood. The people are really nice and friendly. It is really clean around the neighborhood. There is a park nearby and it has a lot of space. I love Middle Village! I always feel safe walking with my dog and the streets and parks are so clean! Pros: A nice residential neighborhood to live in. It's very peaceful and safe here. As someone who grew up here, I can say it's a nice place to raise a family.
Cons: A major downside is that there isn't much to do, the only recreational place to go to is Juniper Park. You have to visit a neighboring town if you want to go somewhere else fun, like the mall.
Not many options for public transportation either. Be warned that the Q38 is super unreliable, you're better off walking to your destination as it's either going to come on time or not at all.

I think overall Middle Village, especially the area in which I live is pretty quiet. One thing. I would definitely like to see more of as a hispanic woman is diversity. For the most part, I feel my neighborhood is safe, however, recently there was a shelter built near a school and children's athletics shelter that many of the residents feel does threaten the safety of the neighborhood. Prior to its construction, many of the neighbors signed a petition to express these concerns. So I do think advocacy and listening to the residents is one area that needs to be improved. Night life is pretty quiet, everyone gets home at around the same time and no one disturbs the peace at too late an hour. The stores are very accessible and employment seems to be very accessible as well. As a senior searching for a summer job, I already have a few stores nearby that offer jobs and I will look into for the summer. Regarding living expenses, I think rent is really high but that depends on the owner.

I have lived in Middle Village for 13 years. This neighborhood has one of the best public school systems surrounding it. There is also a big park called "Juniper Valley Park," where people go to hang out at night or attend mini concerts.

This is a very quiet community. At first I was a little creeped out being surrounded by graveyards but now I love having them nearby. You know they won't build anything on top of them so do not have to worry about overcrowding. When my family comes over and we have the windows open they are shocked that the mostly just hear birds and not the usual noise of a city. We enjoy walking around Juniper Park which is a hidden gem. Very safe neighborhood to live in. You have to own a car around here. Public transportation is very limited (however this makes foot traffic from nonresidents minimal). Limited shops in the area, which again it is better to have a car. Politically a more conservative neighborhood. Neighbors are friendly but I am embarrassed to say can be ignorantly and sometimes blatantly racist.

I’ve been here all 17 years of my life, and there is no where else I would rather live. The people are so kind, supportive, and so very passionate. I’ve connected with many neighbors on various different levels, neighbors of all ages. This is a community where you can truly be yourself, where you can count on one another. The parks and school systems here are like no other. Although there have been disagreements and hardships within the community, this community stays strong and works through it together.

I was born here in Middle Village, raised here in Middle Village, and now as a young adult, still here in Middle Village! It is a nice, quiet, multi-cultural, family oriented neighborhood. We have tree lined blocks and no alternate side parking rules and/or cleaning and yet everyone keeps the area clean! We have a gorgeous park (Juniper Valley Park) with acres of land for all sports, exercise, child's play, and even a dog park! There are deli's, supermarkets, laundrymats, CVS, 7Eleven, Bagel shops, etc. All in walking distance. The area is safe as well.

Safe and quiet neighborhood with friendly neighbors and parking close by. I grew up in Middle Village during the 90's and decided to move back after discovering the affordability. The local business are clean and well maintained such as the local fruit markets and local restaurants. There is a variety of restaurants such as Peruvian and Thai, as well as Rosas Pizza. The majority of people who live in the neighborhood are either small family's or single. Juniper Valley park is in close walking distance from Metropolitan Avenue, which has a basket court and both a soccer and baseball field. The closest mall is the Atlas Park which houses currently TJ Maxx, New York Sports Club, Ashleys Home Store and Regal Cinemas. There is also a small artificial grass area within the mall where during Christmas time a large tree can be seen in the middle. Traffic can be busy especially on Metropolitan Avenue and Central Avenue during peak hours.

My overall experience with East New York has been positive because it is a community that feels like home to me. I appreciate the diversity, the strong sense of community, and the many local businesses, organizations, and programs that support residents. There are a lot of hardworking families and people who genuinely care about improving the neighborhood.
At the same time, I would like to see more investment in the community, especially when it comes to cleaner streets, safer public spaces, affordable housing, better access to quality stores and restaurants, and more opportunities for young people. I would also like to see improvements made without pushing out longtime residents. East New York has a lot of potential, and I think continued investment that actually benefits the people who already live here would make the community even stronger.

I have grown up in east new york since i was 4 years old. I've went to school in my community and have done everything under the sun including party, go out to eat and even just enjoy a bike ride. Loved it, the neighborhood was one of the best neighborhoods I’ve been in. The jobs are great and easy to find. And the parks round the area are always clean.

I don’t live far from East New York, and to be honest, I don’t find the area safe. Not at night and definitely not alone. There’s a heavy presence of drug activity, homelessness, and while you’ll find some working-class families, there are also plenty of people just hanging around, clearly not working. If the city actually plans to develop new housing here, they’ve got a long way to go. Some people might claim they like the area and hey, that’s their tea to sip but I don’t share the sentiment. I’ve been living in Cypress Hills for over four years. It’s slightly different from East New York. I’m not exactly a fan. The area has a large Dominican and Central/South American population, mixed with some Black and West Indian. The noise is loud, especially in the warmer months. And let’s not ignore the drug addicts often half-dressed or passed out near Fulton Street. I honestly don’t get why some people are even listing their homes as Airbnbs around here. The neighborhood isn’t safe.
I like it living here.A lot has changed since we first moved here. It is safer and more developed now. I would like to see the schools and the school lunch improve

I love East New York. As a lifelong Brooklyn resident, my neighborhood is lively and vibrant, filled with a unique spirit. I've always cherished the cultural diversity here. From the music spilling out of windows to the aromas of various cuisines, this mosaic of cultures has taught me inclusivity and respect. I deeply appreciate our strong community. Despite challenges like crime and economic struggles, the resilience of the people inspires me. We look out for one another, rallying during times of need. Neighbors organize food drives, youth programs, and initiatives to keep our streets safe. East New York isn't just where I live; it's part of who I am. Its struggles and triumphs have shaped my character, instilling pride, hope, and belief in the power of community. My experiences motivate me to give back and strive for change, contributing to the growth and success of my neighborhood.

East New York is a cool neighborhood to look in because you never really get bored. Theres restaurants,malls and stores on almost every block. Bus stops and trains are also close and its just a very convenient place to live.

Diverse community: East New York is home to a vibrant mix of cultures, including African American, Caribbean, Latino, and immigrant communities, which contributes to a rich cultural atmosphere.
Public transportation: The neighborhood is relatively well-connected to other parts of Brooklyn and Queens via the subway (A, C, J, Z, and L lines) and buses, making it easier for residents to commute to Manhattan or other areas.
Affordable housing (historically): Compared to other areas of Brooklyn, East New York has been known for more affordable housing options, making it attractive to low-income families and new immigrants.
Community efforts and resilience: Despite challenges, there is a strong sense of community, with numerous grassroots organizations working to improve living conditions and support local residents.

Woodside, Queens, is a delightful family haven, where a walk down the street feels like stepping back in time—way back, like, dinosaur era back. Amidst the charm of Woodside’s neighborly vibe sits Berkeley Cooperative Towers Section 3, an architectural relic reminiscent of the Egyptian pyramids, refusing to join modernity. Their Cooperative Board just denied a request for an electric car charger in their 60+ year-old garage, which seems more suited to horse-drawn carriages or Christopher Columbus’s ship. Electric cars? Not in this Ice Age monument! As Woodside thrives, Berkeley Towers clings to Neanderthal-era policies, pushing its property values to the bottom, while neighboring co-ops embrace the 21st century. But don’t let Berkeley’s windmill-stubbornness fool you. Woodside is a gem, with or without a co-op committed to preserving relics from an era when the idea of an “electric car” was as absurd as a dinosaur in a windmill. Welcome to Woodside—may the voltage be in your favor!

However, I believe there is more need for renovating the neighborhood subway stations, as many can still be found with debilitating conditions, especially the 52nd Street-Lincoln Avenue Station. But despite such concerns, Woodside has been quickly gentrifying as a result of multiple affordable housing lotteries being placed within this neighborhood.

I've lived in Washington Heights all my life, and the one word I'd use to describe it is, hispanic. It's a mostly hispanic neighborhood, that is fairly lower-class, and full of Dominican, Puerto Rican, Mexican, Ecuadorian, Venezuelan, Guatemalan, etc, etc. immigrants( to name a few). It's not the most safe neighborhood, you can see people dealing drugs on some corners of the street, but for any hispanic, it's a haven. A lot of undocumented immigrants live here, and they find their jobs around here doing part time delivery, or side jobs, maybe even construction or manual labor jobs. Most people speak Spanish, which makes it easy to communicate if you are still learning English. As a hispanic person living here, I love it. The location itself of the neighborhood is also great. It's on the west side of Manhattan, so it's directly on the A, C, and 1 line, only 35 minutes away from 42nd st. It's also right next to the Hudson River, and the George Washington Bridge. I love my neighborhood.

Growing up in Yonkers, you quickly learn that this city is so much more than just a suburb bordering New York City. Jersey City has a lot of potential.
One of the most difficult issues is how concentrated poverty limits mobility for certain communities.
Ultimately, my perspective on Jersey City is both appreciative and critical. I value the diversity and the proximity to opportunity, but I also recognize that opportunity is not evenly accessible. The city’s potential is real, but realizing that potential fully requires addressing the deep and persistent effects of concentrated poverty and unequal mobility.

Another thing, they are building condominiums and silk lofts in every empty spot they can find in Bayonne. It is so congested sometimes I feel like I can't breathe.

My overall experience with Bayonne has been incredibly positive. What stands out most is the strong sense of community and the welcoming atmosphere that makes you feel at home. Local businesses, parks, and family-friendly spaces give the city a warm and connected feel, and I appreciate how diverse and supportive the neighborhoods are. Bayonne also offers convenient access to nearby cities while still feeling peaceful and safe. If there is one change I would love to see, it would be continued investment in youth programs, public spaces, and community events that bring residents together even more. Bayonne has so much potential, and I am grateful to be part of it.

I left this dump 25 years ago. That was one of the best decisions of my life. Bayonne used to be an old, dirty, industrial town that was safe and relatively decent to grow up in nonetheless. Over the decades the quality of the town declined rapidly. The streets became dirtier and dirtier. Many stores on Broadway (the main walkable shopping strip) closed. Since there was no place to park, people would fight each other over parking spots. The older generation slowly died or moved out of Bayonne and with them went so many great restaurants, bakeries, stores, etc. For what it's worth, it has attracted many NYC commuters because of its proximity to the city. Some minimal parts of Bayonne have improved, but I would not recommend raising a family there.

I like the environment and how quiet of a place Bayonne is most people know each other. However, the prices for rent have gone up along with the prices for various other things which is definitely inconvenient.

Bayonne is a community growing in size and diversity. While it used to have a suburb feel with great access to NYC life, that quality is decreasing. Becoming over developed and over crowded, it becoming increasingly difficult to carry out daily life without improving things to do or job opportunities.
Bayonne is a good place to live which has a diverse environment, clean town, and calm environment for mental health, especially moving from NYC.

I enjoy the fact that you almost always see someone. Usually it is a familiar face you see. Something I would change is to have kinder drivers, along with lowering the rent especially for residents that were living there before it had increased.
I love how there is everything in Bayonne even though it’s a very small town. You rarely have to go out of Bayonne for stuff.
the environment is serene and very family friendly and oriented, with ease access to services and resources

Overall, Bayonne is a very safe neighborhood and a great place if you have kids. There are many things to do around the city if you're the active type, like going to the gym or the many parks around town. It's a very walkable area so it's easy to commute around if you don't want to use/don't have a car. The light rail is also extremely easy to use as well.

Bayonne is a great city. It is located right next to New York and Jersey City, which makes for short and convenient commutes to work. Within the city, there are many places to go with friends and family, and it is very family-friendly. Everything is within walking distance, promoting less car usage and exercise for residents. I don't think anything needs to change.

I grew up here and since have moved to the Jersey Shore. This town has majorly deteriorated over the past 10 to 15 years. Crime has gone up. Robberies and assaults are now abundant. The commute to New York City is too long, the transportation opportunities are not great. It used to be a wonderful family friendly town. Broadway used to be a beautiful shopping street, now it’s all junk shops. I feel bad because this is where I grew up but I’m so thankful I moved
it is always quite and has some good food restaurants and parks, but there is no night life at all which is boring for most adults.
Bayonne is a very nice area to live in. The community is very safe, and many people know about one another's whereabouts.

I live in The Central area and All I can say is that Clifton is just 10 towns in a trenchcoat. Lived in the Delawanna when I was like 6 and I kinda miss it. There's not a lot to walk to in my area asides from a 7-11 and some doctor's offices. It's a big town which sucks because I CANNOT WALK TO ANYTHING WITHOUT IT BEING A HIKE. It gets BORING at times for a 16 year old. Also SO MUCH STUFF is in North Clifton, which my parents are not comfortable with because It's near Paterson. I've been uncomfortable at the Main Library because I feel like the homeless men are staring at me (North's a shady area) Allwood Library is the Goat tho. This town is very diverse (Great!), with Hispanic, Muslim, and Orthodox Jewish families too! I don't go to the high school but I feel bad for kids who do because there are 3000+ kids there and that must suck. Avoid North Clifton, live in the areas near Nutley and Montclair. We have swap meets in the Allwood sector which is nice! Better than Garfield though!
Great place to live with a wide variety of activities throughout the year to participate in! We feel very safe and informed about what is going on in the city and the surrounding area.

I've lived in Clifton for 8 years now, and it has been really easy to adjust. The neighborhood is nice, there are rarely any crimes that I hear about, and it is very easy to make friends! Everyone is so sweet, places are easy to get to, and you don't have to worry about a far drive for certain things.

Clifton is very close to everything, even the city. It isn't the type of town you can leave your door unlocked, but you can walk to nearby corner stores just fine. There's plenty to do in the day time but most places close before it really gets dark out.

It is a great city that has a welcoming community, many restaurants, shops, homes, schools, and more. Living here has been a an amazing opportunity, especially since I live close to many amazing places like New York City.
Great experience. Living here for 15+ years. Great diversity and culture. Good neighborhoods and people.
Clifton is beautiful and everything about it. I won't like to change anything because Clifton was home to me and still is home to me.

I have a relatively positive relationship with this suburb. The schools, diversity and everything else are great. However, I have been searching for job opportunities for months and it is very difficult to find a entry level job.

I grew up in clifton and i have noticed good and bad things about living here. I appreciated growing up in a very diverse environment and being exposed to different cultures. It was convenient having many stores and restaurant within walking distance. It was even easy for me to walk to work when i worked in customer service. I cherish the friendships i have made here. Some of the downsides is that it's not the safest or quietest place, especially in downtown. Public schools weren't the greatest academically, but there were some extracurricular activities. Traffic has picked up in the past 10 years due to overdevelopment. And now it's almost impossible for my generation to own property here as prices skyrocketed. In order to get the best experience in raising a family here, the household income would have to be on the higher side.
I have lived in Clifton my whole life. I graduated from Clifton High School in 2003. I am currently employed in Clifton.

My overall experience living in Clifton for the 18 years, has had its ups and downs. When I moved here from Paterson it was a bit of adjustment, the school experience for me during my elementary years were rough. I did witness discrimination from my classmates but I out lived throughout my childhood to my current adulthood.

Clifton has a unique charm that blends suburban comfort with urban convenience. I really liked the diversity of cultures you see reflected in the food, local businesses, and community events—it's one of those cities where you can grab authentic Peruvian, Italian, Middle Eastern, or Polish food all within a few blocks.
The parks are another highlight. Garret Mountain and Weasel Brook Park are great spots to unwind, especially if you enjoy nature without straying too far from the city.
What I’d love to see improved is traffic flow—certain intersections and roads like Route 3 can get pretty congested, especially during rush hours. Parking can also be a bit of a hassle in some areas, particularly around Main Ave and the downtown spots.
More community events or open-air markets would be a nice addition too—Clifton has a great local vibe, and expanding spaces for neighbors to gather and support local vendors would really enhance that.
Been living here for 17 years offers, and offerstons of opportunity for children programs and education. Also, plenty to shop around the area.

I've spend all of my life in Clifton, New Jersey ; I've been extremely blessed to live an amazing town like this, from schooling to people to how convenient it is. I feel very safe and accepted in this town, people are very friendly, caring and great to engage with. Schooling is good with good teachers, good programs both during and after school. Many stores to go to with great welcoming staff in almost everyone establishments.

"Clifton was a game-changer! I loved the personalized insights and actionable advice. The assessment was thorough, and the results were spot-on. I'd like to see more resources for implementation and a mobile app for easier access. Overall, a valuable tool for personal and professional growth!"

Clifton is very diverse, there’s people of all different religions and ethnicities everywhere you go. The safety really depends on where in Clifton you are at but for the most part, it’s extremely safe. I would say the neighborhoods is in the middle of all the fun stuff like the malls and shopping centers.

I had a fantastic experience with Clifton, NJ! As a visitor, I was impressed by the city's warm hospitality and abundance of amenities. Here's my feedback:

My experience with Clifton is a good perspective I have with them. The place is clean and organized. Many oppurtunities you have here like jobs. Place is very calm to the point where you could go out for runs around the block. Schools are good and in a nice enviorment. For the most part in clifton is a nice calm place to come and live.
What I really like about Hawthorne is the town park. Goffle Brook Park is very big with multiple fields, a lake, and beautiful creeks flowing throughout the park.

I grew up in Hawthorne. I have moved away several times for various reasons but have always found myself coming home. Its a small town but its home. The downside of Hawthorne is there are to many people and they're building apartment buildings yearly making it more congested on the roadways and in the schools.

Hawthorne is a small town that prefers to stay that way. The people and town are conservative leaning overall. Has decent amount of public transportation via a couple bus routes and a train station. The changes that have occurred recently in the last 10 years have improved the real estate value. Apartment complexes made to house more people. Not many chain restaurants or stores. Infrastructure for water, electricity, and gas is maintained well enough for few instances or outages in severe weather storms. A predominately white town that has seen an increase in the Hispanic population recently so diversity is improving.
hawthorne has been a very inviting neighborhood since I recently moved a month ago. Commuting into the city is a breeze with a train nearby. People are friendly and make me feel at home and welcome.

Hawthorne is mainly split into two parts and there's a clear contrast between them. One side is well kept and green. The other is dirtier and the houses seem worn down. Perhaps Hawthorne can do better in cleaning the trash and maintaining the roads on the downtown area of Hawthorne.
Hawthorne is a very diverse small town with an excellent public schooling system. It’s a perfect mix of having a nightlife but with some beautiful parks.
Its not bad, there's the good and the bad. The public schools probably need the most work especially in athletics. They should use their athletics to promote and get more students to come here.

I've lived in Hawthorne for over 20 years. I grew up nearby in Glen Rock and though GR is ranked highly, I feel that my children will not suffer educationally or socially by living here. There are far fewer McMansions and finance professionals; just real people working real jobs trying to live comfortably and provide for their families.
Houses are a bit closer together than towns in Bergen county, but that means less lawn to cut! Taxes are still reasonable (for NJ), and I don't feel like I am being punished for choosing to remain in the state.
A few things I would change are: restrict overnight parking on roads, mandatory odd/even on road parking (to alleviate road cleaning during winter), add speed bumps to roads to discourage the speeders flying down the road, and find ways for older home owners to receive assistance in upkeep (some people cannot maintain their property due to illness, etc. and should not be punished, but assisted - this helps them and the town.)

The council is awful. Been here 20 years and every employee is a miserable jerk. Very poor communication and very bad management of the town and borough. Never met a single decent person who worked in the borough. Its towns like this why so many are fleeing to Florida.
Hawthorne is a very close-knit community which is a great environment to grow up in. The people are friendly and there are many community activities throughout the year.
I am a resident of Hawthorne and I can truly say that it is a very safe community. The schools are excellent as well. When I have kids I would love to send them to school here.

I have lived in Hawthorne for nearly 16 years. I truly enjoy living in our town and all that it has to offer - 2 miles of walking paths throughout a beautifully restored park, town pool and tennis courts, a dog park, amazingly delicious restaurants! The overall friendliness of the town is terrific. As a real estate agent, I have helped 7 families move to Hawthorne, and all are happy that they did.
Must say it has it all with a down to Earth feel. Last of the true small towns. I really should be giving a bad review so nobody finds out.
Overall is a quiet and friendly town. It could use more restaurants that are catered towards the younger adults and teens.

Hawthorne, New Jersey is a blend of the traditional and non-traditional, as there is a balance between the friendly, conservative Baby boomers and the Millennial newlyweds. Whereas the suburb is quiet, as its only semblance of nightlife is Shortway's Barn on Goffle Road, rest assured that safety is guaranteed by its hardworking police department. Hawthorne has a Bergen County atmosphere for a Passaic County price.

I like Hawthorne. It's a friendly, fun town! There are always new places opening up. I would change the public school system. We have the best education for special needs students, but the public schooling for everyone is not great. I also wish Hawthorne embraced homeschooled students more.

Migrating in United States last year was one of the greatest change in my life. I moved to Hawthorne, New Jersey. I love this suburb because it's peaceful, quiet, and clean. I live near Goffle Brook Park, let me tell you it's beautiful in there. You see the change with the trees when season changes. The Italian places in Hawthorne are really good. The disadvantages are transportation, i don't really see bus in here but there's a train but it's far. Also, it's hard to find jobs here when you're an associate's degree.
It does not offer much and the taxes are going up. This town is very cliquey and is changing in a negative way. The schools are not even close to the surrounding towns.

Hawthorne is a lovely, polite little town - everyone either knows you or wants to get to know you. Great restaurants, solid library, connected community; the only downside is that it is decently heavy with conservatives, and most voters (on both sides) don't turn out on election day.

I grew up and work here. Many Latinos, very small town. Everyone knows everyone. Great place to eat. It is a very easy commute to NY or anywhere in NJ because of the NJ Path system. Can watch soccer at the arena too.

I enjoy how quiet and generally well knit the community is despite being heavily influenced by the urban lifestyle surrounding it. Despite the rapid pace and near consant flux of commuters passing through in order to take the PATH into New York City there is very little I would change about my hometown. The roads in particular need to be better maintained.
Very safe town, a lot of restaurants, parks, quiet place, but commute is difficult when there are games in the Red bull arena stadium and parking spot are difficult.

Living in Harrison has been a wonderful opportunity. Commuting to other towns by bus or train is very reliable. There are many grocery stores with nearby access. The parks are fairly clean and there is good access to books in the library. Rent tends to be somewhat high in Harrison, making it difficult for low-income families to continue living in the area.

Harrison is becoming like a second Hoboken in a good way. Downtown Harrison is filled with newer expensive apartments, and more of these apartment buildings are being built throughout the town and in neighboring towns. This part of Harrison is a very city like, and beautiful and modern. There is also a PATH Train Station in Harrison which is very convenient for transportation to NYC, Jersey City, and Hoboken. The public schools in Harrison are also fairly well, as I’ve gone to Harrison Schools for many years I can say the teachers are excellent in Harrison. Harrison needs help with expanding this environment ALL throughout the town.

Grew up and lived in town 30+ years. Recently moved out and don’t miss anything about it. Traffic is worse after gentrification of a square mile town. Township doesn’t care about long term residents and also the history of this town has eminent domain on it for profits and the town has lost its soul. I went through the education system in town from kindergarten to graduating high school. Education system wasn’t even average. But seems like it has improved as of late.

Harrison has been on a continuous rise since 2019! Everything from new buildings to beautiful parks to great local and modern restaurants is right here in Harrison. Looking for a little more excitement ? Hop on the path and you’re a 15 minute ride to NYC.

It’s kinda nice, not really much crime until you get closer to Newark and even then, it’s the residential area. Small town where nearly everyone knows each other and also nearly everyone is Hispanic/Latino. Not much to do though, there’s a park and a recreational center, and maybe some bars but that’s all. Kearny is a nicer town but more crime.
Ugly old buildings becoming gentrified
Lots of Restaurants, bars ,Bodega s ,coffee shops and near the NJ Path Trains ,close to Newark , and not far from Jersey City overall nice place to live

Small beautiful town. Close to everything like Rutgers, NJIT, Walmart, Pharmacies, Restaurants, Gyms, parks, gyms, path train to NYC etc..
I have lived in Methuen, Livingston, Edison, Jersey City and Harrison is still my favorite place when to overall diversity, walk ability, commute to NYC, air port access, restaurants etc
Its a hidden gem!!
Harrison is a overall safe and tight nite town. Many folks living in Harrison have been here for generations and care deeply about the prosperity of the town and its people.

An awful place to “live” and to visit. One of the biggest dumps in the country. Total disaster on its best day. You have to visit here to really appreciate what a horrible place it is. Should be condemned. Actually makes Kearny look decent and that says a lot. Why would anyone who works in the city live in Hsrrison and not Montclair? Doesn’t get worst. Deserves zero stars

A hidden gem that 20 mins to 30 mins into NYC a train ride. It's a very safe community and everything you want within walking distance or driving... Walmart is 5 minutes drive , there are gyms close by, new restaurants, a beautiful Park (hudson park) that offers a nice and challenging run or work out with ample space and tennis court. Alot professionals people mixed with college students going to rutgers etc... Its 15 minutes away to Newark Airport... Its a beautiful town... Traffic can be a pain in the butt sometimes, but that is not that bad.
I have lived in Brooklyn, Queens, Edison, Metuchen and have access to all amenities but I miss Harrison to be honest. It's not too crowded, it's not too hipster, it's not too expensive, it just right...

My family has been renting in Harrison for a few years. The bigger 3+ bedroom apartments are in multi-family houses owned by a certain generation of people who revel in being landlords. I don’t know much about the modern apartments, but they seem nice. The PATH station was recently remodeled and looks great, but it’s a bit treacherous getting there as a pedestrian or cyclist. Car traffic overwhelms the main avenues and there are no bike paths. For the most part, the town does a good job of keeping the streets clean and they’re fantastic at clearing the snow. Every once in a while the town is engulfed in an awful odor like rotten eggs or burning plastic. I think it’s something to do with the landfill downwind of us. It’s not the prettiest place. It feels transient and lacking community, like a place created by cynical investors to exploit workers.

Very walkable. Best bedroom community to access downtown Newark. Excellent public services. PATH, NJ Transit, Rt. 280, Turnpike exit 15W access in town. Crime rate very low. Extremely diverse. Gentrifying quickly. Home of Red Bulls Soccer arena, many restaurants. Real estate market is red hot. Large hispanic/brazilian/chinese/New York commuter influx. Retail and commercial development is booming. Similar to Hoboken, Jersey City in that street parking is tight. Only downside to Harrison is public schooling: large ESL population results in standardized test score depression. It's an ideally located bedroom community for jobs in Newark, Jersey City and downtown NYC.

Harrison is boring. No nightlife at all and what is available to go to isn’t very nice. I have to say they have yummy Portuguese and Peruvian places to eat, but that’s the high point. Many longtime Caucasian residents are most definitely racist but try to play it off as if they aren’t. Many have the mentality and way of being that is very “Staten Island” if you catch my drift. Heroin and cocaine is a problem with many of its longtime residents. I had issues once trying to get a cab when I arrived from NYC on the Path train and had to visit family. This could have been a nice place to live. The sad thing is they are turning this ultimately very industrial area to a residential area and buildings, instead of areas for recreation, are popping up at every corner, regardless of the fact that people are leaving! A sad example is how residents from surrounding buildings are using a garage to take walks because there are no easily accessible parks/trails and whatever they are doing near the waterfront is not easy to access you have to walk to cross 4 lanes with barely safe traffic measures. Last time i tried we had to cross a highway bridge to get over to a park that is minutes away. Potholes worst than anywhere else. Its disgusting all the building being done and the lack of accommodation for space. People are stuck working from home and allll you can hear and see is constction everywhere. If it were not for building amenities it would be unliveable. With COVID now, living in Harrison is no cup if tea.

affordability and parking are my only issues. I love the diversity of the town. The crime rate is low. I love the local businesses. It is a great location and offers public transport. I feel safe raising my family here.

For the most part, Harrison is very safe. The town highly respects and honors its police workforce and firefighters. Parts of Harrison are next to Newark but even Newark is beginning to gentrify. Although the town is slowly diversifying, it does have heavy Hispanic influence. The schooling is rather adequate compared to school systems in other towns. Out of all schools, most of the funding and effort is put into Harrison High School. The quality of students and teaching is rather debatable, as the school is ranked #7,456 nationally and #235 in NJ (by US News). Not to mention, the hiring process for public schools are quite influenced by nepotism and favors alumni of their schools. However, the upside is that the community and culture of the schools are very close and compact; it feels like a grand family. The night life of Harrison is quite dull. The town was a fine place to grow up in. However, there are surrounding towns with better qualities such as Secaucus or Montclair.

I am extremely dissatisfied with living here. One of the biggest issues is the persistent sewer-like odor, which makes the environment unpleasant and uncomfortable. No one should have to deal with such an offensive smell in a place they pay to call home. Another major concern is the lack of adequate parking. Finding a parking space is consistently frustrating and inconvenient, especially when returning home after a long day. Residents should not have to struggle to find somewhere to park near their own homes. Between the unpleasant odors and ongoing parking difficulties, living here has become more stressful than enjoyable. These issues significantly affect the overall quality of life and make it difficult to feel comfortable in my own living environment. For the amount of money residents pay, basic expectations such as a clean, odor-free environment and reasonable parking accommodations should be met. I would not recommend living here based on my experience.

I really love Newark, some people might disagree with me. I believe this is a city where many people can say they have grass-roots. There are many opportunities here for people who come from low-income families. Also, the food here and in New Jersey in general is just delicious. Not like any other place here in America. I do believe that it is less safe than some other cities but honestly, no where in America is completely safe.

Overall, Newark isn't too bad of a place to live in. Yes, there are safer areas to live in, and yes, there is better education systems and healthier areas elsewhere.
