Being a resident here since I was little, I was able to find a community within my own home, one that provides fun and an abundance of shared laughs whilst also making sure people get the education needed. North Star Academy, for example is a primary example, providing a wealth of education for those less fortunate. It's not the best, but it is home.

Newark is a great city. It very hectic in the morning times and calm during the night. Newark is a place where a lot of people grow up and become stars. There is never a dull moment and it is not hard to find your group of people in Newark. Some places in Newark could be cleaner and need to be fixed up, but otherwise Newark is a great place to live in.

I am a Newark native born and raised for 32 years. All I know is this city of Newark. From my fun childhood, teenage, young adult-hood. Newark is home from me and others. Newark is Beautiful to me, it's not perfect which gives it hope and continuous opportunities for improvement and growth. This city seems to always amazes me with the privilage of job opportunities I had the chance to experience, networking, going to school here and further my education at Essex County college and Rutgers University, which I am planning on completing my Masters in Public Administration and Affairs at. Newark is diverse and full of culture and opportunity. I would like to see more investment in safety, cleanliness, and youth programs.

Not the best place to raise a family. I would like to see more cleanliness. Keeping drugs and alcohol off the streets. I would like to see less people banging around on corners and more people getting jobs and going to school.

It’s a large city that definitely needs support from local authorities. That being said, there is obvious growth, and the people are doing their best with what they have. It has a lot of opportunity, beautiful architecture, and nice parks. Just needs some help.
I grew up in Newark, it has its good things and bade things. Overall it depends on how you use your experience there.

I love my city for how convenient it is everything is 15 minutes to 1 hour away from Major cities like NYC or Philly. In Newark there is place all around from every type of culture if I wanted to try it I can. Sometimes some place aren’t the best but overall there is a lot to do here or close by that it’s hard to ever want to move from here.

My overall experience with Newark hasn't been anything captivating or moving. But there are select few places that will move you, like views downtown during a sunset. I love the city skyline downtown, I also love the food and cultural diversity. Although Newark could use a bit more work.

Moving to Newark was an experience filled with both challenges and growth. At first, the change felt overwhelming. Everything was unfamiliar—the streets, the pace of life, and the way people carried themselves. There were moments when the city felt loud and intimidating, and adjusting to a new environment wasn’t easy. Seeing struggle up close made me more aware of the realities many people face every day, and at times it felt heavy to carry that understanding.
However, Newark also showed me strength, culture, and resilience. I met people who were hardworking, supportive, and proud of where they came from. The sense of community, the diversity, and the determination I saw in others pushed me to work harder and believe in myself. Living in Newark taught me how to adapt, stay focused, and appreciate growth even when it comes from discomfort. While the move wasn’t perfect, it helped shape who I am today and gave me a deeper appreciation for perseverance and opportunity.

I am a Newark native and am proud to be from this city. From the culture, to education, to ease of transportation and diverse food choices, it's a city to fall in love with. What I would like to see change or develop is improvement of cleanliness in busy/urban areas, better traffic flow and more funding for community events and local artists.

I love my city, Newark, and I love some of the opportunities it provides for young adults. However, homelessness is a huge problem in my city. These vagrant people need help, and no one is doing anything to help. The streets also aren't kept clean often, and this creates an unsafe and unfriendly environment. I hope that in the future, this problem is solved and my community is much better. Also, there is a lot of gun violence putting people in danger. I hope all of these changes.

Overall i think Newark needs to stop just building new apartments that cost way too much. The cost of living is too expensive, once can barely afford a one bedroom that isn’t in a safe place and looks up to date.

Newark is really that hit or miss state. The reputation Newark has is something a lot of people hear about, the violence, the justice, the society within, the people. It really depends on what part of Newark you're from. I'm close to the Ironbound, Essex Country, and while we've had our fair share of incidents here and there, it's really an area where they keep to themselves. There isn't much diversity as some may think. It's really filled with with Hispanics, Latinos, and those from Brazil and Portugal.

A diverse place. Similar to NYC, without all the crowdedness and expensive prices. It's a huge city with many community events and party scenes with people who wholeheartedly care about the place they live.

Living in Newark has been a challenging experience for me. The apartment building I live in could definitely be in better condition, and overall, the living conditions aren't always ideal. The public school system also leaves a lot to be desired unless you're able to get into a private school, which isn't an option for everyone. The streets are rough, and there's a constant feeling of needing to watch your back. As a young woman, walking around alone often feels unsafe and anxiety-inducing—I almost never do it. I spend most of my time indoors because it's where I feel the safest.
As a Newark resident, I truly hope to see more change, especially when it comes to safety. I want to be able to walk outside without fearing for my life. Everyone deserves to feel secure and at peace in their own community.

My overall experience with Newark has been a mix of both challenges and growth. What I really like about Newark is its diversity—you can meet people from all over the world, and that brings a lot of culture, different perspectives, and good food! There’s also a strong sense of community in many neighborhoods, and it’s clear that people care about where they live and are working hard to make it better.
That said, there are definitely things I’d like to see change. Safety can still be a concern in certain areas, and I think more community programs and youth engagement opportunities could really help. I’d also love to see more investment in education and job training programs—especially for people who are just starting over or coming from other countries, like I did.
Overall, Newark has a lot of potential. It's a city with a rich history, a lot of heart, and some real momentum for positive change. I’m hopeful for its future.

There are different parts of the city. I live in the area that is more family oriented and maintained well. The city does a great job in hosting community events. There are a lot of offerings for children of all ages.

In Morris Plains, I love the small and tight-knit community and the ability to see familiar faces everywhere I go. They raise people with kindness which spreads throughout the community.
Lovely neighborhood with friendly faces. Convienient stores at every corner! Safe neighborhood and trustworthy schools

Extremely nice location to live, with great connection to both highways and other main facilities. Great stores and places to live, with somewhat affordable and rising home prices. Amazing schools nearby, and great town nature and environment in general.

The biggest question is that is this area safe for children and families and I have great news, it truly is great for families and children. This area and other near have events for adults and children that are always fun to participate in. In addition, this area is truly safe, you hear a little bit about crimes and stuff.

I love Morris Plains because of how perfectly suburban the town is. I absolutely love the diversity we have in Morris Plains. Not only are the people diverse, but even the architecture of the buildings surrounding us are unique. So long as you do a little research, it is very easy to plan a lovely day with a cherished one without breaking the bank. In addition, the local businesses we have really add to the overall feeling of unity. It is like a large family here in Morris Plains. Great place to live for families. Good school system complimented by beautiful houses and scenery, multitude of restaurants and food joints, and an abundance of things to do, from museums to parks. The standard of living is quite high.

The town is dirty half done projects everywhere. How many times do you have to fall on the sidewalks before they fix them. The police don't investigate anything. They ride around all day blowing a tractor horn. Don't waste your money.

My overall experience was a plesant one , it's a very lovely place with people of different ethnicities, everyone was kind and respectful, there was also resaurants and cafes nearby.

Westport is a great place to live if you're wealthy and white and have children with no special needs. First, education. Yes the schools here have a great reputation, until you have a special needs child; then the schools tend to fail miserably. Also, repeated incidents of racism and antisemitism have plagued the schools especially the high school in recent years. There never seems to be any punishment made public in this cases; the town keeps them quiet. Second, traffic. The traffic is TERRIBLE. And it gets continually worse. Because I95 is always backed up, people cut through the main arteries in town thinking that they'll save time. All they do is clog the main arteries with increasingly heavy traffic for longer periods of every day. Now add all the cyclists in the nicer weather and it's a nightmare. Restaurants are overrated and expensive; go to Fairfield or Norwalk for better dining. Cost of living is outrageous. People ARE snotty and rude and cut lines in stores, it's true.

Westport is a very snooty town with a lot of people that will shove their money and assets down your throat. The people can be very unfriendly at times, and the atmosphere comes off as cold and unwelcoming. There has also been a history of racism and discrimination at their pubic schools, with several instances of racial slurs being verbally directed and shared against students of color.
This town also has an infamously high cost of living that makes it hard for growing families to afford the area unless they’re pursuing a high paying job.
And on top of this, the town severely lacks third places outside of your usual clothing stores and fast food restaurants that the younger crowd can spend time in and socialize. It feels as if almost every kid, teen, and young adult here is cooped up in their giant home unless they’re at work or at their local McDonald’s.

I grew up in the small town of Mine Hill, next to Dover. We had our own elementary school and would be transferred to a nearby middle school through a choice program, where we apply for seats in the neighboring towns. Although I didn't attend the middle school, I attended the high school. At first I was nervous due to the bad rumors circulating, but once I was there, it was completely different. The majority of the population of Dover are minorities. It felt inclusive as we are able to share our cultures and experiences that were very similar yet so different. The city of Dover had a reputation that they weren't as good as the other prestigious schools around them, due to having a high population of immigrants, but, having experiencing it myself, they are a strong community that can hold their own against those who try to put them down. I taught in Dover HS for a short period of time and was appalled at how bad the school system in Dover is. My only recommendation to any potential home buyer in Dover is to see the high school in person. DO NOT trust the numbers that are reported. I have taught in schools all over NJ and Dover is like nothing else. Students are crammed into classes that are at capacity, and in many cases there are more students than capacity so they just bring the class into the lunch room and do nothing for a period. It's a very sad state of affairs. Also, many students, and I mean many, don't speak English at all, so the teachers basically give up trying to teach, which is why so many teachers are fleeing from Dover. Look at the teacher vacancies online for yourself.
In terms of the town itself, the properties are way overvalued. Moving a little further west will get you a cheaper house with a better school system and only add a few minutes more to your commute. Also the train is not reliable.

It's a quaint little town with a number of novel conveniences, a comfortable compact nature that allows for a lot of on-foot travel (which is much appreciated for saving on gas costs), and it's at a great location, connecting a number of similarly interesting locations along the train line to New York City. It is a beautiful and great up an coming small city by the Hudson River with great diversity, and many historical old homes with amazing original architectural designs. The city has been in a state of revival for years and it hasn't let up yet. It is a very safe city with great Police and Fire Departments. It also has the Metro North station close by that takes you into the city in only an hour, and if you feel like hiking you have the Bear Mountain State Park only fifteen minutes away. It's truly the best of both worlds.
great town! I was born in Peekskill and everything is available to me and near by. they are also improving as well.

Bridgeport, Connecticut, is a city undergoing a complex evolution and fascinating diversity. This city has historic sites, such as Barnum Museum and the Beardsley Zoo. There are various tourist destinations for visitors and residents to explore around the city. Bridgeport boasts a strong sense of community and diverse cultural offerings, which I have found very engaging. However, the experience can be different due to the consistent urban development and a revitalization of downtown storefronts that are used to attract more businesses and activity. Some changes can include the improvement of public transportation and reliability on it, for it would make a significant difference in daily life and enhance connectivity across neighborhoods. Overall, Bridgeport offers a rich cultural tapestry, but faces challenges in infrastructure and economic development that, if addressed, could unlock its full potential.

Bridgeport has become more than just a place to live, it's our home. Buying our first home here, marked an important chapter in our lives. Since then, we've put down roots, started a family, built a community, and found a strong sense of stability. Renovating our home, each project feeling like an investment in our future. Being part of a loving and supportive community has made this experience even more meaningful.
What truly sets Bridgeport apart from other areas in CT is its diversity. The city reflects a rich mix of cultures, and backgrounds that can be seen throughout its neighborhoods, local businesses, and community events. This diversity adds depth to everyday life and is especially meaningful for parents, allowing children to grow up exposed to different cultures, perspectives, and traditions.
Bridgeport is a city with resilience and a genuine sense of community growth. For our family, it represents belonging, growth, and pride. It has truly become the place we call home.

I have lived in Trumbull since the second grade and attended Trumbull public school from elementry through high school. I would highly reccomend the area for families seeking a strong education system and supportive community. The town is friendly and offers many after-school activities and volunteering oppertunities for students.
I personally participated in the local swim team, which was a positive experience that taught me sportsmanship, discipline, and perserverance. The only drawback was growingup there were limited restraunts and activities in the area, but I have seen the town gradually improve and become more modern over time.

The neighborhoods feel safe, and there are plenty of parks and walking trails that make it easy to stay active and enjoy nature. The schools and local services seem well organized, and everything is conveniently located, from grocery stores to restaurants. I especially appreciate how close it is to surrounding areas while still maintaining a quiet suburban atmosphere. Overall, Trumbull offers a comfortable balance of calm living and accessibility that makes it an enjoyable place to be.

Great little town with a cool beach vibe and easy access on the ferry to nyc. Really enjoyed the coffee shops and restaurants on the main strip

We moved here in retirement. We’ve found the neighbors friendly and helpful. People passing on the street greet you. The town is very “walkable”, and the stores are convenient. There have been many opportunities to become involved in the community. We pay less in taxes than we did in North Jersey, and housing prices seem to be lower for sure than N Jersey. We take the ferry into NYC, parking is free, and it’s a pleasant experience. There’s a walking/cycling path right at the water and beaches are close. The surrounding area is beautiful to drive through. We’re glad we happened on this town!

Literally, everything is “two blocks away!” Coffee, the harbor, art gallery, bay beach, first-run cinema, library, post office, shops, restaurants, school, places of worship, senior center, you name it! We chose it for the ferry, which takes you right to Manhattan, and we’re on NJTransit bus line and Hudson Trail bike path. The best part, though, is our neighbors. We feel so lucky to live in this town.
I love the downtown area, proximity to the water, small suburb feel. I’d like more stores on First Ave and to clean up the feel of Route 36

Atlantic Highlands is an extremely safe neighborhood with a ton of family life. The little town holds a variety of restaurants, as well as an adorable coffee shop on their main street named First Avenue. While venturing throughout this town you can visit the waterfront and their marina which holds many boats as well as the seastreak to New York. At night you can see the glowing lights of the city, and to wrap it all up you can grab an amazing scoop of ice cream from Nicholas Creamery! Although the town is little, is offers so much and remains a safe, happy community even in the roughest times. You will always feel welcome when visiting this town due to the warm people that reside in it. Atlantic Highlands is the beginning of the Jersey Shore and is only 10 minutes away from the coast line. Living here is a dream. The variety in weather makes this quaint town extravagant. Hopefully more people will visit soon!

Atlantic Highlands is a great town to live in whether you are single, have a family, or looking to just get away from the fast pace of the city. It is a town full of history with older buildings, and older passage ways. The nightlife could be considered as about average due to the lack of bars, but has an abundance of great restaurants that are all EXCELLENT. The bay being so close is a huge plus as well, adding a scenic view to the "beachy" town vibe as well. Though, it is quite expensive to live here and the taxes are now astronomical compared to earlier years. Though, due to the high prices and high demand to live here, is an example of how great it is to live here. It is extremely safe to live here, as well as being extremely family friendly due to the amount of parks and amazing public school system (whether it be Middletown, or Atlantic Highlands/Highlands). The job opportunities in the immediate area are a little scarce, but due to the ferry, it is an easy commute to NYC.

text: North Bergen, NJ has been my home for two years, and the best thing about it is the easy accessibility to Manhattan—buses, ferries, and tunnels put Midtown within a half hour while I enjoy a quieter, more affordable life on the Jersey side. In these two years I’ve watched real estate progress firsthand, with new developments, renovations, and rising property values signaling a town on the rise. Still, I’d love to see the culture grow to match. I hope for more art-connected events—galleries, murals, live music, and festivals that celebrate our diverse community and give local artists a stage. I’d also welcome a safe, vibrant nightlife: well-lit, well-run venues where people can go out and come home feeling secure. Most of all, I’d love an expanded local job market, with more companies, support for small businesses, and opportunities that let residents work close to home instead of commuting out.

They invited local artisans to showcase their crafts, from handmade jewelry to intricate woodwork. Food stalls offered a variety of delicious treats, including fresh seafood caught right from Norwalk’s waters.
